cues.text: Told he was too small
Jamie Vardy grew up in Hillsborough, a part of Sheffield in England.
He loved the local club, Sheffield Wednesday, and he played in its youth teams.
But when he was sixteen, the club let him go.
They thought he was too small.
Flip the sign.
For a while, Jamie stopped playing football altogether.
Many people would feel hurt if they were told they were not big enough.
But one club’s opinion did not decide what he could become.
Being small, or being told no, doesn’t decide who you will become.
Work and football
After a break, Jamie started playing again for Stocksbridge Park Steels, a small club far below the big leagues.
He earned £120 a week there.
He also had a job as a technician, making medical splints that support injured arms and legs.
Pull the tab to move the splints along.
Jamie worked at his job and played for his team, and he kept getting better.
He made it into the first team, and in the end he scored 55 goals for the club.
Doing your best in a small place still counts. Hard work is never wasted.
A door that stayed shut
In 2009, bigger clubs noticed him, and Jamie spent a week on trial with Crewe Alexandra.
But the move did not happen, and he stayed at Stocksbridge.
Many people would want to give up after another no.
Knock on the doors.
In 2010, Neil Aspin, a manager who had admired Jamie for a long time, signed him for FC Halifax Town.
Jamie was the team’s top scorer with 25 goals, and his teammates voted him their Players’ Player of the Season.
Keep going after a no. Sometimes the right person is behind the next door.
One step at a time
In 2011, Jamie moved up a level, to Fleetwood Town.
He scored 31 league goals, the most in the whole division, and Fleetwood won the title and their first-ever promotion to the Football League.
Climb the steps.
In 2012, Leicester City signed him for about one million pounds, a record fee for a player from outside the Football League.
Jamie was twenty-five.
Many players reach big clubs as teenagers, but his path was longer, one step at a time.
Your path can be slower than other people’s. Every step still takes you forward.
When he nearly quit
Jamie’s first season at Leicester was hard.
He lost his form, and some supporters criticised him online.
He even thought about leaving football.
Lift the flap to see who helped.
His manager, Nigel Pearson, and the assistant manager, Craig Shakespeare, convinced him to stay.
The next season, Jamie scored 16 league goals.
Leicester won the Championship and were promoted to the Premier League, and his teammates voted him their Players’ Player of the season.
When you feel like giving up, talk to the people who believe in you.
Champions of England
In the 2015–16 season, Jamie scored in eleven Premier League matches in a row, a new record.
Leicester were the underdogs, a team few people expected to win, but they became the champions of England.
Flip the scoreboard.
Jamie was named the Premier League Player of the Season, and he played for England too.
The boy who was once let go for being too small had kept going, all the way to the top.
Everyone grows in their own time. It’s never too late to keep going.
